headline: No documented interaction pathway: both agents are local-only, non-networked, and expose no shared channels or writes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, browser, or subprocess surfaces, and pathway likewise exposes no clipboard/files/stdin-stdout channels. With no shared communication channel or ingestion path, prompt injection between the pair is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared clipboard, file mount, or MCP bridge, injection risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared clipboard and shared folders.
Do not add an MCP bridge between them.
Review any future orchestrator for automatic message forwarding.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither LightZero nor pathway has network egress, filesystem read/write, or documented data classes touched, so there is no evident route for sensitive data to flow from one agent to the other or to a third party. The pairwise leakage pathway is blocked by the profiles as given.
conditions: IF either agent is granted filesystem access or network egress in a future deployment, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled for both agents.
Avoid mounting sensitive workspaces into either agent.
Recheck data-class handling before enabling any file inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles show no filesystem write, no git mutation, no subprocesses, and no network egress. Since neither agent can modify shared mutable resources, there is no capability overlap that can create write-write conflict in the current configuration.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later grants both agents write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk appears.
mitigations: Do not point them at the same writable workspace.
Use separate sandboxes if write access is added later.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing system and pathway is document-processing, but neither profile shows action-taking authority, external I/O, or a documented pipeline where one agent's output is automatically trusted by the other. Without an explicit handoff channel, cascading error is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF pathway is configured to consume LightZero outputs as authoritative inputs without verification, cascading error becomes possible.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step between agents.
Require schema validation on any exchanged output.
Do not auto-execute downstream actions from model text.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, and both profiles show no network egress or file surfaces that would create a residency, retention, or regulated-data transfer issue. With no identified sensitive data flow, there is no compliance mismatch to assess from the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's inputs, compliance controls must be checked against the deployment region and retention policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document any future retention settings before deployment.
Review residency requirements before enabling external connectors.
